note: Illinois DNR park south of Marshall, on 146-acre Lincoln Trail Lake. Two campgrounds about 650 m apart off the park road: Lakeside fills a wooded peninsula on a bluff above the lake and has a tent area; Plainview, inland, has the long pull-throughs. The shower buildings close November 1 to May 1. --Claude
summary: DNR camping/park pages, ExploreMoreIL (Lakeside 100 + Plainview 111 units) and the 2027 fee PDF read. 172 electric sites (Lakeside 72, mostly 20-30 ft back-ins; Plainview 100, 40-ft back-ins + 11 pull-throughs to 45 ft) + 11 non-electric, 30 A with 50 A at ~25, no water/sewer at sites; showers (Nov 1 - May 1 closed), water, dump. 2027 Electric $28 (stored $11 was the tent class; surcharge/reservation fee cleared). Booking operator -> usedirect #!park/39. Waterfront lakefront -> lakeview recommended (pads on a wooded bluff 14 m above the lake, 40-65 m back). Phone 217-826-2222 (none stored).
flags: WATERFRONT: recommend lakefront -> lakeview (at most). The stored evidence ('079L-089L on narrow lake peninsula ~25-50m from shore') is right on distance but not on access: the nearest Lakeside pads, 45L 39.34142,-87.71609 and 44L 39.34132,-87.71585 (~40 m from the north arm), 78L 39.33987,-87.71935 and 79L 39.33978,-87.71952 (~45-50 m), 83L 39.33944,-87.72027 (~65 m from the west shore), sit under continuous canopy on a bench ~14 m above the water (3DEP 179 m at 45L and 178.6 m at 79L vs the lake at ~165 m, reached within ~45 m: a ~30% wooded slope). That is a climb-down bluff behind a treeline, which disqualifies lakefront. Whether the lake shows through the trunks can't be confirmed from summer imagery; if a human wants the strict default-down call, not waterfront. Plainview is 300 m+ from any water.
